blocks.text: Venturo respects copyright, trade marks & other intellectual property rights.
This Copyright & Intellectual Property Policy explains:
how intellectual property displayed through Venturo is treated;
the rights Venturo has in its own original material;
how third-party intellectual property may appear on Venturo;
the responsibilities of Users & Activity Providers;
how copyright or intellectual property concerns can be reported; and
how Venturo may respond to infringement complaints.
This Policy should be read together with the:
applicable Business or Activity Provider Terms.

Different intellectual property rights may apply to different types of material.

Copyright ownership does not necessarily depend on whether a copyright symbol appears on the work.
Users should therefore not assume that material found online is free to copy simply because it does not contain a copyright notice.
Unless otherwise stated, original material created by or for Venturo and owned by Venturo may include:
photographs commissioned or created for Venturo;
original database arrangements or compilations where protected; and
These materials may be protected by copyright, trade mark law or other applicable intellectual property rights.
Venturo may display the following notice on its website, application or other material:
© 2025 Viatori Ventures (Pty) Ltd trading as Venturo. All rights reserved.
This notice applies to original material owned by Venturo.
It does not claim ownership of third-party content, trade marks, photographs, logos or other material that belongs to another rights holder.
Users may access & use Venturo Content for ordinary personal, non-commercial use associated with the Venturo Platform.

This permission does not transfer ownership of Venturo intellectual property to the User.
Unless permitted by applicable law or expressly authorised by Venturo, Users may not:
reproduce substantial portions of Venturo Content;
copy Venturo descriptions for use on another directory or platform;
build a competing database using Venturo Content;
falsely suggest an association with Venturo;
copy Venturo software or source code; or
use Venturo intellectual property in a misleading or unlawful manner.
Requests for permission may be sent to:
The Venturo name, logo & other distinctive brand elements may be protected under applicable trade mark, copyright or other intellectual property law.
Use of Venturo branding must not:
falsely suggest that another business is Venturo;
falsely imply sponsorship or endorsement by Venturo;
confuse customers regarding the source of a product or service;
imitate Venturo in a deceptive manner; or
damage or misuse Venturo's intellectual property rights.
Where permission to use Venturo branding has been given, the branding must be used in accordance with any applicable brand guidelines.
Venturo displays the names, brands, trade marks & logos of independent businesses as part of its activity-discovery services.
Ownership of those trade marks & brands remains with the relevant rights holder.
Displaying a business name or trade mark on Venturo does not mean Venturo owns that intellectual property.
It also does not automatically mean that Venturo operates the relevant business or activity.

When an Activity Provider submits content to Venturo, the provider must have the necessary rights or authority to allow Venturo to use that material.
The applicable Business or Activity Provider Terms may grant Venturo permission to:
use it within the Venturo app & website;
feature it in relevant Venturo collections; and
use it to promote the relevant business, activity or Venturo service in accordance with the agreed licence.
Submitting content to Venturo does not automatically transfer ownership of that content to Venturo.
An Activity Provider submitting material to Venturo confirms that it has the necessary permission to do so.

other intellectual property that it is not authorised to provide.
Where a rights dispute arises concerning provider-supplied Content, Venturo may temporarily remove or restrict the disputed material while the matter is investigated.

By submitting content to Venturo, Users grant Venturo the licence described in the Venturo Terms & Conditions to host, store, reproduce, display, format & distribute that content as reasonably necessary to operate the Venturo Platform.
Users must only upload material that they have the right to share.
Material being publicly accessible online does not automatically mean that it is free for commercial reuse.

Venturo does not treat the fact that Content appears on Google, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, another directory, a business website or another public website as permission to copy or commercially reproduce that Content.
Where Venturo wishes to reproduce third-party creative material, it should have an appropriate right, licence, permission or other lawful basis for doing so.

Where Venturo creates editorial descriptions from researched information, Venturo should use its own original wording rather than reproducing substantial portions of another business's marketing copy.
The appearance of factual business information on Venturo does not mean Venturo claims ownership of the underlying business, brand or third-party intellectual property.
Photographs may be protected by copyright.
Venturo should therefore use photographs where an appropriate right to use them exists.
photographs commissioned by Venturo with appropriate usage rights;
photographs submitted by an Activity Provider under an appropriate licence;
content made available under a licence that permits Venturo's intended use; or
other photographs Venturo is legally authorised to use.
Attribution alone does not necessarily create permission to use a photograph.
A photograph, video or post appearing on a public social-media account remains subject to applicable rights.
Venturo should not assume it may download & republish social-media content commercially simply because:
the business appears in the photograph;
another account has reposted it; or
the material can be downloaded or screenshotted.
Where social-media content is to be reused by Venturo, appropriate permission or a lawful licence should be obtained where required.
Venturo may use third-party content made available under Creative Commons or another recognised licence where the licence permits Venturo's intended use.
Venturo must comply with applicable licence conditions.

A licence should be checked before the Content is published.
If you believe Content appearing on Venturo infringes copyright that you own or are authorised to represent, please contact:
Your notice should provide sufficient information for Venturo to investigate the complaint.

evidence reasonably supporting ownership or authority;
any relevant original source or publication information; and
confirmation that the information provided is accurate to the best of your knowledge.
If you represent the rights holder, Venturo may request evidence that you are authorised to act on their behalf.
If you believe Venturo Content improperly uses a trade mark, business name or other protected brand asset, contact:
an explanation of the alleged infringement; and
your authority to make the complaint where you act for another party.
When Venturo receives a sufficiently detailed intellectual property complaint, it may:
review records relating to the Content's source;
contact the User or Activity Provider that supplied the Content;
replace the Content with authorised material;
restore Content where the complaint is not substantiated; or
Removal during an investigation does not constitute an admission of infringement by Venturo or another party.
Where disputed Content was submitted by a User or Activity Provider, Venturo may provide that party with sufficient information about the complaint to allow them to respond.
Personal information will be handled in accordance with the Venturo Privacy Policy & applicable law.
Where a User or Activity Provider believes Content was removed incorrectly, they may provide Venturo with information supporting their right to use the Content.
details showing the Content was independently created; or
Venturo may reconsider its decision after reviewing the information supplied.
Venturo may restrict or terminate access for Users or Activity Providers that repeatedly submit Content that infringes third-party rights.
Depending on the circumstances, Venturo may:
More serious infringements may result in immediate action.
Intellectual property complaints should be made in good faith.
A person must not knowingly submit false information, impersonate a rights holder or misuse Venturo's reporting process to remove legitimate Content.
Venturo may refuse to action abusive complaints and may take appropriate action against Users who deliberately misuse the reporting system.
Venturo may maintain records relating to the origin & permitted use of Content.
These records may be used to investigate intellectual property complaints.
An Activity Provider may contact Venturo if it believes information or Content associated with its business should be corrected, replaced or removed.

Venturo may verify the request before changing or removing Content.
A business listing appearing on Venturo does not transfer ownership of the business's intellectual property to Venturo.

Businesses may request corrections to inaccurate factual information without acquiring ownership of Venturo's original Platform Content.

If Venturo becomes aware that its Content, branding, software or other intellectual property is being used without authorisation, Venturo may take appropriate steps to protect its rights.
Depending on the circumstances, this may include:
reporting infringement to the relevant platform;
pursuing other remedies available under applicable law.
This Policy is governed by the laws of the Republic of South Africa.
Relevant intellectual property rights may include rights arising under South African copyright, trade mark, design & other applicable laws.
Where Content or intellectual property is used internationally, rights under other jurisdictions may also apply.
Venturo may update this Copyright & Intellectual Property Policy as its Platform, Content features or legal obligations develop.
The latest version will be made available through the Venturo website.
The effective or last-updated date will appear at the beginning of the Policy.
